statements.t: We will continue to increase our discretionary marketing spend, including account-based, targeted demand generation and brand spend, to drive the effectiveness of our sales teams.
As a result, we expect our total operating expenses to increase as we continue to expand.
We will also continue to build out a single, unified platform, simplify customer onboarding and service usage, and simplify our pricing and packaging.
We will also need to expand, retain, and motivate our sales and marketing personnel in order to target our sales efforts at larger enterprises and senior management of these potential customers.

We intend to continue expanding our efforts to attract customers outside of the United States by augmenting our sales teams and strategically increasing our presence in a number of markets in select international locations.

In addition, we cannot be certain what actions the United States or another country’s government may take with respect to certain of our customers that may adversely affect our ability to do business with our customers that operate in China, target China as a market or that have strong business ties to China, and any such governmental action could have a negative impact on our business.
While the conflicts are still evolving and the outcomes remain highly uncertain, we do not believe these or other conflicts will have a material impact on our business and results of operations.
We expect our revenue growth to be dependent on an expanding customer base and continued adoption of our offerings.
In anticipation of winning new customers and staying ahead of our customers’ needs, we plan to continue to invest in order to expand the scale and capacity of our software-defined modern network.
Our customers require constant innovation within their own organizations and expect the same from us.
Therefore, we will continue to invest in resources to enhance our development capabilities and introduce new products and features on our platform.
We believe that investment in research and development will contribute to our long-term growth but may also negatively impact our short-term profitability.
We will continue to invest in our network infrastructure by strategically increasing our POP locations.
We also anticipate making investments in upgrading our technology and hardware to continue providing our customers a fast and secure platform.
If we have server asset levels in excess of forecasted network capacity needs, we have in the past and may need to continue to write-down or write-off server assets.

If the supply of certain components upon which we rely is further disrupted or delayed, there can be no assurance that we will be able to obtain adequate replacements for the existing components or that supplies will be available on terms and prices that are favorable to us, if at all.
Over the long term we expect cost of revenue to decrease as a percentage

Our gross margin has been and will continue to be affected by a number of factors, including utilization of our network, the timing of our investments in the expansion of our network, which can increase depreciation and colocation costs in advance of expected demand, our ability to manage our network service providers and cloud infrastructure-related fees, the timing of amortization of capitalized software…
Over the long term we expect gross margin to increase as we continue to drive efficiencies in our operations and increase our revenue.
Over the long term we expect our research and development expenses to decrease as a percentage of our revenue.
Over the long term, we expect our sales and marketing expenses to decrease as a percentage of our revenue.

In the near term, we expect to continue to incur costs associated with supporting the growth of our business, including international expansion, but expect these costs to decrease as a percentage of our revenue over the long term as we continue to drive efficiencies in our operations.
We expect to maintain this valuation allowance for the foreseeable future.

We have generated losses from operations in the past and may continue to incur operating losses for the foreseeable future due to the investments and strategic initiatives we intend to make to grow our business.

As of September 30, 2026, we were in compliance with the covenants described in Note 8 to the condensed consolidated financial statements in Part I, Item 1 of this Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q, and we expect to continue to be in compliance for at least the next 12 months.

To the extent that there are material differences between these estimates and actual results, our future financial statement presentation, financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows will be affected.
